summary.headline: Kewal Kiran Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12.4% YoY to INR 325 crore and FY26 EBITDA margin hit 19.6%, prompting a raised 20% three-year CAGR ambition.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 12.4% YoY to INR 325 crore and FY26 revenue reached INR 1,212 crore, up 20.9%. Q4 EBITDA was INR 62 crore (up 18% YoY) and FY26 EBITDA was INR 238 crore (up 25%), with margin above the 17-18% guided range at 19.6% for the year. Management raised its growth ambition from 15% to 20% CAGR over three years, with about 15% organic and the balance from acquisitions, and said Kraus contributed to growth. Q&A covered the war-related raw material risk, working capital, store additions, gross margin band, and the Goregaon land monetisation, which remains under negotiation.

segments.name: Killer
segments.commentary: Double-digit FY26 sales growth; 457 EBOs; Q4 SSG 6.8% and FY26 SSG 9.4%.

segments.name: Kraus
segments.commentary: Growth upwards of 20% in FY26; EBITDA margin in line with KKCL; EBOs expanded to 28; focus shifting to working capital cycle. Company is 50% owner with no change to stake for first five years.

segments.name: Lawman
segments.commentary: Repositioned toward D2C model; now operates 90 EBOs; robust FY26 sales growth.

segments.name: Integriti
segments.commentary: Notable growth in Q4 and FY26 after price strategy change; gaining counters in multi-brand and chain stores.

segments.name: Junior Killer
segments.commentary: High FY26 sales growth in kidswear; brand gaining traction.

guidance_outlook: Organic growth guided at 15-18%; with inorganic contribution the three-year CAGR ambition is 20%, from 15% earlier.
Acquisitions may not materialise uniformly each year; no specific target or deal identified.
Net store additions of 50-70 EBOs in FY27, mostly franchise (about 85% franchise / 15% COCO).
Gross margin to stay in 41-43% range going forward.
Capex of INR 30-35 crore per year, covering front-end and back-end.
Working capital to stay within 130-140 days overall; Kraus structurally higher.
Standalone traditional business growth expected to be upward of 15% as Lawman and Integriti pivots scale from Q1 FY27.
Exports expected to remain flat or decline next year due to Middle East disruption.
capex_capacity: Capex guidance INR 30-35 crore annually, including front-end and COCO stores.
Kraus manufacturing fully outsourced; no plan to use KKCL standalone capacity in the immediate future, as KKCL is running at full efficiency.
Net EBO additions of 50-70 in FY27; company-owned share about 15-20%, franchise about 80%.
Company added net 57 EBOs in FY26, taking total to 666 stores as of March 31, 2026.
demand_pricing: No price hike taken yet; management says there is room to raise prices if needed.
GST cut from 22 September passed fully to consumers in Q3; management calls FY26 impact neutral, with differences by brand.
E-commerce growing in line with company growth.
Denim share about 48% of mix; management expects mix to stay around current levels (45-48%).
Raw material and war-related cost pressure: management said it may absorb 1-2% of profit hit rather than lose revenue; no channel price revision yet.
Exports are under KKCL brand names, mainly to Middle East and Saudi Arabia; disrupted over the last three months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on monetising the Goregaon land?
qa_highlights.answer: Still under negotiation with no decision; management will update quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 20% growth target split between organic and inorganic?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic 15-18%, with the remaining close to 5% from acquisitions over a three-year period.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and why is Kraus higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall limit 130-140 days; Kraus higher because of LFS and retail skew and manufacturing WIP of 50-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin band?
qa_highlights.answer: 41-43% going forward, with mix shifts due to price bracket changes.

qa_highlights.question: Will other income continue at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 decline was mark-to-market; annualised other income guided at INR 30-35 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Not under consideration; promoter holds about 74%, and the company is not thinking about buyback currently.

risks_watch: Raw material cost inflation from the war (oil and cotton); management may absorb 1-2% profit hit.
Acquisition execution risk: no deal identified, and the 20% CAGR relies on about 5% from acquisitions.
Receivables rose from about INR 170 crore to INR 320 crore over two years, per analyst; management says working capital is within 130-140 days.
Export disruption in Middle East and Saudi Arabia; exports expected flat or lower next year.
North region underperformed expectations; management focus on West and South.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and margins, but evasive on acquisitions, pricing response to war-driven costs, and the Goregaon land deal, where answers were deferred to future calls.
key_quotes: We aim to further accelerate the growth target from 15% CAGR to 20% CAGR in the next three years and it is expected to be meaningfully supported by a well-defined acquisition framework.
As of now our endeavor was to not lose the revenue and we should not reduce our market share.
Even if we have to take a hit of 1% or 2%, the company is ready to take that kind of hit.

adds.what: Net 50-70 EBO additions in FY27, mostly franchise (~85% franchise / 15% COCO)

growth.why: Organic growth guided at 15-18% for FY27 (midpoint 16.5%), with three-year CAGR ambition raised to 20% including acquisitions, but no specific acquisition identified; backing is partial via 50-70 net EBO additions, Lawman/Integriti pivots and INR 30-35 cr annual capex, while exports are guided flat to down.
